name: Hana Fūma
equipment: Grappling hook and 50 ft. silk cord
A crow-mask token of the Fūma clan
Common clothes for blending into a crowd
features: Expertise (double proficiency on Stealth and Sleight of Hand)
Sneak Attack (1d6 extra damage when you have advantage or an ally is adjacent to the target)
Shinobi Hand-Signs (Thieves' Cant — secret signed and coded language of the ninja clans)
Criminal Contact (Spy feature: a network of informants and a reliable contact)

personality.traits: I am quiet as falling snow and twice as cold to those who cross me. 🦊 I trust shadows more than people, and I always know where the exits are. A joke at the right moment hides a great deal.
personality.ideals: Freedom. I bowed to a clan-master once and learned what loyalty bought me. Now I answer to no daimyō and no shōgun — only to the price agreed and the word I choose to keep.
personality.bonds: The Fūma clan raised me, trained me, and sold my sister to settle a debt. I work the shadows to gather coin and leverage enough to buy her back — or to burn the clan to the ground.
personality.flaws: I cannot resist a locked box or a guarded secret, even when prying it open will get me killed. And I struggle to let anyone close enough to betray me, which means I am very often alone.

appearance: A small, wiry woman of Hinomoto who moves like smoke through a doorway. Her black hair is bound back tight and her dark eyes miss nothing — flicking to hands, to blades, to shadows. ⚔️ She favors close-fitting shinobi garb of charcoal and midnight blue, soft-soled tabi boots that make no sound, and a scarf she can pull across her face in a heartbeat. Kunai ride in sheaths along her forearms and thighs, and a lacquered crow-mask hangs at her belt. In a crowd she becomes utterly forgettable; in a dark alley she becomes the last thing you never saw.
backstory: Hana was born into the Fūma, one of the hidden shinobi clans that sell secrets, sabotage, and silent death to the warlords of the floating world. From childhood she learned the arts of the shadow-walker — climbing, lockcraft, poisons, the coded hand-signs by which ninja speak without sound. She was a prized agent, slipping into castles to read a lord's private letters or to leave a single kunai on his pillow as a warning. Then the clan-master, pressed by a gambling debt, sold Hana's younger sister to a coastal pleasure-house to balance the books, and called it duty. Hana walked away that night and never looked back. Now she takes contracts on her own terms — espionage, theft, the occasional knife in the dark — building a war-chest of coin and blackmail. Some of it she means to spend buying her sister's freedom. The rest, she suspects, she is saving for the day she finally settles accounts with the clan that raised her and sold her blood.
